const canvas = resolveCanvas(spec);
    const value = nearestRatioForAspect((rect.w * canvas.width) / (rect.h * canvas.height));
mutations.after:
const canvas = resolveCanvas(spec);
    const value = nearestRatioForAspect(rect.w / rect.h);
mutations.because: The frame's fractions read as an aspect without multiplying them back through the canvas — the mistake is invisible on a square canvas, where w/h and (w*W)/(h*H) agree exactly, and a 1:1-only test would pass. It is wrong on every other canvas: a top-half frame on 9:16 is 1.125 (nearest 1:1) and this mutant calls it 2.0 (nearest 16:9), so the run asks for a wide picture to fill a nearly-square box. Caught by the caller test that asserts all three ratio cells at once, which is why that expectation is deliberately NOT uniform.
command: a framed ground asks for the box's shape, not the canvas's
